epic.title: EPIC-050: Natural Answer Collection and Parsing
epic.functionalNeed:
The analysis asks each AI engine to return its answer in a fixed structure instead of answering the way it would for a real user. This changes the answer itself (wording, nuance, length), so the analysis measures a constrained response, not what users read. With this EPIC each engine answers naturally, and the analysis reads that raw answer to derive the rankings, competitive outcomes, themes and sources it needs, so the product keeps the same metrics on real answers.

[CHANGED 27 OCT] The answers are also collected the way a real user sees them. Today every engine is called through its API (through OpenRouter), and that answer is not what a user reads in the engine's interface: on the test set below, the sources of an API answer and of the interface answer to the same prompt overlap only 7% to 18%, and the API route costs about seven times more per answer than managed rendered capture. Collection becomes route by engine. Public, no-login surfaces (logged-out ChatGPT and Gemini) move to rendered capture; Claude and Grok stay on their official API because their interface sits behind a login; Perplexity stays on its API while no capture vendor can reach it (one vendor is in outage, another has stopped its Perplexity service). Every answer is stored raw so it can be read again, and each country keeps getting its own answers.

A rendered answer cannot be forced into a schema, so one reader serves every route: the same rules turn an API answer and a rendered answer into the metrics the product consumes. The Google surfaces (AI Overviews, AI Mode) use this capture and this reader; adding them stays in their own EPICs. The switch to rendered capture in production waits for the legal sign-off and the vendor contract. The natural API route ships first, without waiting for capture: each later switch of an engine to capture has no marker on trends either, and clients are told by email.

The reading rules below come from a test set of 499 answers collected on 20 Oct 2026 (18 test prompts and 12 prompts of a client analysis, through the engines' API without our instruction and through their rendered interface). In that set, most answers use bullets, headings or tables, about half of the visibility answers are split into "best for" sections, they name a median of 5 brands instead of 10, and two head-to-head answers out of three do not pick a single winner. The answers, their labels and the decision register are in this Drive folder, with a README for the dev team: [Dataset](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_rS2XnVbI0z5DL97YFSMqRO_d2i4rg2V )  
  
For now the parsing needs to work on this dataset, as we are still waiting for the legal confirmation on UI scraping. In any case the parsing needs to work on both sources: the API natural answer from OpenRouter AND the UI scraping from the provider, with the same output. Read the README of the folder first: it lists every file, route and label.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Engines answer questions naturally
acceptanceCriteria.statement: As a user trusting the analysis, I want each engine to answer questions the way it naturally would for a real user, so that what I see reflects genuine engine behavior and not a constrained, artificial response.

criteria.text: Given a question is sent to an engine, When the engine answers, Then it produces its natural response without being forced into a predefined output shape
criteria.given: a question is sent to an engine
criteria.then: it produces its natural response without being forced into a predefined output shape

criteria.text: Given an engine's natural answer, When it is recorded, Then the raw answer is preserved, meaning the full response of the engine or the vendor (answer text, search results and citation positions), not the text only, so it can be reviewed and re-parsed if needed
criteria.given: an engine's natural answer
criteria.then: the raw answer is preserved, meaning the full response of the engine or the vendor (answer text, search results and citation positions), not the text only, so it can be reviewed and re-parsed if needed

criteria.text: Given the same question asked to the same engine, When compared, Then the analyzed answer matches the kind of answer a real user would receive
criteria.given: the same question asked to the same engine
criteria.then: the analyzed answer matches the kind of answer a real user would receive

criteria.text: [CHANGED 27 OCT] Given an analysis whose AI insights language is not the language of the country (eg: France - French with English insights), When a question is sent to an engine, Then the engine gets no instruction on the language of its answer, so it answers in the language of the question, as a real user in that country would read it. This removes the rule added by GEO-918 that asks the engine to write its answer in the AI insights language.

Given an Other-type prompt or a Category Topics prompt of an unbranded analysis, When it is sent, Then it is sent naturally too and its answer is read like a Perception answer (themes), while the setup calls (category and competitor discovery, prompt adaptation) keep their structured request
criteria.given: an Other-type prompt or a Category Topics prompt of an unbranded analysis
criteria.then: it is sent naturally too and its answer is read like a Perception answer (themes), while the setup calls (category and competitor discovery, prompt adaptation) keep their structured request

criteria.text: [CHANGED 27 OCT] Given natural answers in the language of the country, When GEO writes its own text from them (AI summaries, key concepts and themes), Then that text is in the AI insights language, as today

acceptanceCriteria.title: Derive structured results from the natural answer

criteria.text: Given a natural visibility answer, When it is parsed, Then the brand ranking and the other entities mentioned are extracted from it, and the ranking only holds brands that the answer names
criteria.given: a natural visibility answer
criteria.then: the brand ranking and the other entities mentioned are extracted from it, and the ranking only holds brands that the answer names

criteria.text: Given a natural competitive answer, When it is parsed, Then its outcome for each brand is extracted from it (story 1.5), and not a ranking of the brands
criteria.given: a natural competitive answer
criteria.then: its outcome for each brand is extracted from it (story 1.5), and not a ranking of the brands

criteria.text: Given a natural perception answer, When it is parsed, Then the perception themes and their sentiment are extracted from it
criteria.given: a natural perception answer
criteria.then: the perception themes and their sentiment are extracted from it

criteria.text: Given any natural answer that cites sources, When it is parsed, Then the cited sources are extracted with their links
criteria.given: any natural answer that cites sources
criteria.then: the cited sources are extracted with their links

criteria.text: Given a raw answer from any collection route, whether an engine answering naturally through its API or an answer captured from a rendered surface, When it is parsed, Then the same structured results are extracted regardless of how the answer was collected; GEO-1498 displays them, so any change to these results during the build is agreed with GEO-1498 first
criteria.given: a raw answer from any collection route, whether an engine answering naturally through its API or an answer captured from a rendered surface
criteria.then: the same structured results are extracted regardless of how the answer was collected; GEO-1498 displays them, so any change to these results during the build is agreed with GEO-1498 first

criteria.text: Given a natural answer, When it is parsed, Then the full answer text is stored with its formatting (paragraphs, lists, headings, tables) so it can be displayed as the engine wrote it
criteria.given: a natural answer
criteria.then: the full answer text is stored with its formatting (paragraphs, lists, headings, tables) so it can be displayed as the engine wrote it

criteria.text: Given a natural answer that names brands, When it is parsed, Then each mention of the tracked brand and of each competitor is identified in the text, including the other names an engine uses for a brand (eg: "Claude" for Anthropic), so the display can highlight them and link each ranked or chosen brand to its first mention
criteria.given: a natural answer that names brands
criteria.then: each mention of the tracked brand and of each competitor is identified in the text, including the other names an engine uses for a brand (eg: "Claude" for Anthropic), so the display can highlight them and link each ranked or chosen brand to its first mention

criteria.text: Given a natural answer with inline citation markers, When it is parsed, Then each marker is linked to the source it points to, so the display can number the markers and the sources the same way, and two markers that point to the same page resolve to one source
criteria.given: a natural answer with inline citation markers
criteria.then: each marker is linked to the source it points to, so the display can number the markers and the sources the same way, and two markers that point to the same page resolve to one source

acceptanceCriteria.title: Recognise the brand in a natural answer
acceptanceCriteria.statement: As a user, I want my brand to be recognised in a natural answer whenever the engine names it or one of its products, and only then, so that my visibility reflects what a real user reads.

criteria.text: Given a natural answer, When it names the brand or one of its products (eg: "Brooks Adrenaline GTS" for Brooks), Then the brand counts as named, using the same brand family as the Actions Center (the brand, its spelling variants, sub-brands, products and regional names)
criteria.given: a natural answer
criteria.when: it names the brand or one of its products (eg: "Brooks Adrenaline GTS" for Brooks)
criteria.then: the brand counts as named, using the same brand family as the Actions Center (the brand, its spelling variants, sub-brands, products and regional names)

criteria.text: Given a brand known under a former name since a rebrand, When the answer uses only that name (eg: "BoursoBank" for Boursorama), Then the brand family groups it under the brand and the brand counts as named
criteria.given: a brand known under a former name since a rebrand
criteria.when: the answer uses only that name (eg: "BoursoBank" for Boursorama)
criteria.then: the brand family groups it under the brand and the brand counts as named

criteria.text: Given a brand that appears only in a source title, a link or a cited domain, When the answer text never names it, Then the brand counts as not named
criteria.given: a brand that appears only in a source title, a link or a cited domain
criteria.when: the answer text never names it
criteria.then: the brand counts as not named

criteria.text: Given a natural answer, When it is parsed, Then the whole answer text is read, including a closing question to the user, so a brand named in that question counts like any other mention
criteria.given: a natural answer
criteria.then: the whole answer text is read, including a closing question to the user, so a brand named in that question counts like any other mention

criteria.text: Given a name shared by several companies (eg: "On", "Nickel", "Boots"), When it appears, Then the analysis decides from the context (the category, the brand website) whether it is the brand
criteria.given: a name shared by several companies (eg: "On", "Nickel", "Boots")
criteria.then: the analysis decides from the context (the category, the brand website) whether it is the brand

criteria.text: Given a visibility answer that names the brand with a negative or mixed tone, When it is parsed, Then the brand counts as named, and no tone is extracted or shown for visibility answers, as today
criteria.given: a visibility answer that names the brand with a negative or mixed tone
criteria.then: the brand counts as named, and no tone is extracted or shown for visibility answers, as today

criteria.text: Given a natural answer, When it names retailers as places to buy (eg: "available at REI, Zappos or Amazon"), review sites, media, places, generic product types or brands of another category, Then they are kept out of the ranking and of Share of Voice
criteria.given: a natural answer
criteria.when: it names retailers as places to buy (eg: "available at REI, Zappos or Amazon"), review sites, media, places, generic product types or brands of another category
criteria.then: they are kept out of the ranking and of Share of Voice

criteria.text: Given an answer that names more than 10 brands, When it is parsed, Then every brand counts as named for Visibility and Share of Voice (the top-10 cap of GEO-1255 goes), and Average Position keeps ranks 1 to 10
criteria.given: an answer that names more than 10 brands
criteria.then: every brand counts as named for Visibility and Share of Voice (the top-10 cap of GEO-1255 goes), and Average Position keeps ranks 1 to 10

criteria.text: Given the tracked brand or a configured competitor, When the answer names it, Then it always counts as a brand, whatever its type (a retailer or a review site can be a client)
criteria.given: the tracked brand or a configured competitor
criteria.then: it always counts as a brand, whatever its type (a retailer or a review site can be a client)

acceptanceCriteria.title: Rank brands in a natural answer
acceptanceCriteria.statement: As a user, I want the ranking of a natural answer to follow how the answer presents the brands, so that the position I see is the one a real user perceives.

criteria.text: Given a natural answer, When the brands are ranked, Then the rank of each brand family is the order of its first mention in the answer, intro sentence included, so the first brand named is number one
criteria.given: a natural answer
criteria.then: the rank of each brand family is the order of its first mention in the answer, intro sentence included, so the first brand named is number one

criteria.text: Given an answer with list numbers, "best for" sections or a table, When the brands are ranked, Then the answer still gets one ranking by order of first mention, and the list numbers or section labels do not change it
criteria.given: an answer with list numbers, "best for" sections or a table
criteria.then: the answer still gets one ranking by order of first mention, and the list numbers or section labels do not change it

criteria.text: Given an answer that names several products of the same brand, When the brands are ranked, Then they fold into one entry for the brand at the position of its first mention, and each product keeps its own row in Brand Rankings with the position of its own first mention
criteria.given: an answer that names several products of the same brand
criteria.then: they fold into one entry for the brand at the position of its first mention, and each product keeps its own row in Brand Rankings with the position of its own first mention

criteria.text: Given an answer that names no brand at all (eg: neighbourhoods only for a hotel question), When it is parsed, Then the brand counts as not named, the answer is left out of the Share of Voice denominator, it stays out of the question status as today (GEO-835), and the question panel shows the answer with the verdict "No brands named" and no ranking rows (display in GEO-1498); "Unranked" keeps its current meaning (no engine names the brand)
criteria.given: an answer that names no brand at all (eg: neighbourhoods only for a hotel question)
criteria.then: the brand counts as not named, the answer is left out of the Share of Voice denominator, it stays out of the question status as today (GEO-835), and the question panel shows the answer with the verdict "No brands named" and no ranking rows (display in GEO-1498); "Unranked" keeps its current meaning (no engine names the brand)

acceptanceCriteria.title: Read the competitive outcome in four buckets
acceptanceCriteria.statement: As a user, I want each head-to-head answer to say whether the engine chose my brand, chose it only in some cases, or did not choose it, so that AI Choice reflects how engines really answer competitive questions.

criteria.text: Given a natural competitive answer, When it is parsed, Then it gets one of four outcomes for the tracked brand: Chosen, Conditional, Not chosen or Overlooked, and the brand or brands the answer picks are stored with it
criteria.given: a natural competitive answer
criteria.then: it gets one of four outcomes for the tracked brand: Chosen, Conditional, Not chosen or Overlooked, and the brand or brands the answer picks are stored with it

criteria.text: Given an answer that picks the brand with no condition (eg: "the best pick from this set is Timberland" for Timberland), When it is parsed, Then the outcome is Chosen
criteria.given: an answer that picks the brand with no condition (eg: "the best pick from this set is Timberland" for Timberland)
criteria.then: the outcome is Chosen

criteria.text: Given an answer that picks the brand because the engine found nothing on the other brands, When it is parsed, Then the outcome is Chosen
criteria.given: an answer that picks the brand because the engine found nothing on the other brands
criteria.then: the outcome is Chosen

criteria.text: Given an answer where the brand wins at least one condition (eg: "Choose Dr. Martens if you live somewhere wet, sloppy, and rainy... Choose UGGs if your winter is mostly dry and freezing cold"), When it is parsed, Then the outcome is Conditional
criteria.given: an answer where the brand wins at least one condition (eg: "Choose Dr. Martens if you live somewhere wet, sloppy, and rainy... Choose UGGs if your winter is mostly dry and freezing cold")
criteria.then: the outcome is Conditional

criteria.text: Given an answer that calls the brands equal, or names the brand among joint winners, When it is parsed, Then the outcome is Conditional
criteria.given: an answer that calls the brands equal, or names the brand among joint winners
criteria.then: the outcome is Conditional

criteria.text: Given an answer that picks another brand, a brand outside the question, or does not name the brand, When it is parsed, Then the outcome is Not chosen
criteria.given: an answer that picks another brand, a brand outside the question, or does not name the brand
criteria.then: the outcome is Not chosen

criteria.text: Given a conditional answer where the brand wins no condition, When it is parsed, Then the outcome is Overlooked
criteria.given: a conditional answer where the brand wins no condition
criteria.then: the outcome is Overlooked

criteria.text: Given a conditional answer, When it is parsed, Then only the outcome is stored, not the condition each brand wins: the user reads why in the answer
criteria.given: a conditional answer
criteria.then: only the outcome is stored, not the condition each brand wins: the user reads why in the answer

criteria.text: Given an answer where the engine declines to pick or rejects the question, When it is parsed, Then it is not counted, like a refusal (story 1.6)
criteria.given: an answer where the engine declines to pick or rejects the question
criteria.then: it is not counted, like a refusal (story 1.6)

criteria.text: Given a question framed negatively (eg: "Which brand isn't just greenwashing"), When it is parsed, Then the outcome follows the conclusion of the answer and never the order in which brands are named
criteria.given: a question framed negatively (eg: "Which brand isn't just greenwashing")
criteria.then: the outcome follows the conclusion of the answer and never the order in which brands are named

criteria.text: Given a competitive answer, When it is parsed, Then each configured brand of the question gets its own outcome, so one conditional answer can be Conditional for both brands of a head-to-head
criteria.given: a competitive answer
criteria.then: each configured brand of the question gets its own outcome, so one conditional answer can be Conditional for both brands of a head-to-head

criteria.text: Given an unbranded analysis (no tracked brand), When a competitive answer is parsed, Then every brand of the question gets its outcome and the brand or brands the answer picks are stored, so the display can show the winner
criteria.given: an unbranded analysis (no tracked brand)
criteria.then: every brand of the question gets its outcome and the brand or brands the answer picks are stored, so the display can show the winner

acceptanceCriteria.title: Stay resilient when a natural answer cannot be fully parsed
acceptanceCriteria.statement: As a user, I want the analysis to behave predictably when an engine's natural answer cannot be fully interpreted, so that one unparseable answer does not corrupt or block the rest of my analysis.

criteria.text: Given a natural answer that cannot be fully parsed, When it is processed, Then the parts that can be extracted are kept and the parts that cannot are recorded as unavailable rather than guessed
criteria.given: a natural answer that cannot be fully parsed
criteria.then: the parts that can be extracted are kept and the parts that cannot are recorded as unavailable rather than guessed

criteria.text: Given an answer that yields no usable structured data, When the analysis aggregates results, Then that single answer is excluded without failing the question or the analysis
criteria.given: an answer that yields no usable structured data
criteria.then: that single answer is excluded without failing the question or the analysis

criteria.text: Given one extraction that failed on an answer (eg: the ranking or the competitive outcome), When the metrics are computed, Then that answer is left out of the metric the extraction feeds, and is not counted as unranked or not chosen; today such an answer counts as not named, so this applies to new analysis dates only
criteria.given: one extraction that failed on an answer (eg: the ranking or the competitive outcome)
criteria.then: that answer is left out of the metric the extraction feeds, and is not counted as unranked or not chosen; today such an answer counts as not named, so this applies to new analysis dates only

criteria.text: Given parsing produces a result, When it is stored, Then the raw answer remains available so the extraction can be corrected and re-run later
criteria.given: parsing produces a result
criteria.then: the raw answer remains available so the extraction can be corrected and re-run later

criteria.text: [CHANGED 27 OCT] Given perception themes, When they are extracted, Then each answer is read in full, not cut, and a failure applies to the country and category being extracted, as the extraction runs per country and category

Given an extraction that failed (eg: perception themes), When the next analysis run happens, Then the new run extracts it again from its own answers, and the analysis date where it failed keeps the extraction as unavailable
criteria.given: an extraction that failed (eg: perception themes)
criteria.then: the new run extracts it again from its own answers, and the analysis date where it failed keeps the extraction as unavailable

criteria.text: Given an answer that is cut before its end, a refusal to answer, or an empty answer, When the metrics are computed, Then it is left out of every metric (today it counts as not named, new dates only), and the question panel shows it as not counted for that engine (display in GEO-1498)
criteria.given: an answer that is cut before its end, a refusal to answer, or an empty answer
criteria.then: it is left out of every metric (today it counts as not named, new dates only), and the question panel shows it as not counted for that engine (display in GEO-1498)

criteria.text: Given an answer that does answer the question but names no brand, When it is processed, Then it is not a refusal and follows the rule of story 1.4
criteria.given: an answer that does answer the question but names no brand
criteria.then: it is not a refusal and follows the rule of story 1.4

acceptanceCriteria.title: Preserve existing metrics and downstream views
acceptanceCriteria.statement: As a user, I want all existing dashboards, rankings, and source views to keep working after this change, so that moving to natural answers does not regress anything I already use.

criteria.text: Given an analysis produced with natural-answer parsing, When it is opened, Then every existing view renders in the same form, without missing data attributable to the change
criteria.given: an analysis produced with natural-answer parsing
criteria.then: every existing view renders in the same form, without missing data attributable to the change

criteria.text: Given natural visibility answers, When Visibility is computed, Then it is the share of counted answers that name the brand
criteria.given: natural visibility answers
criteria.then: it is the share of counted answers that name the brand

criteria.text: Given natural visibility answers, When Average Position is computed, Then it stays the mean rank over the answers where the brand is named, ranks 1 to 10, with no penalty when the brand is absent, as today
criteria.given: natural visibility answers
criteria.then: it stays the mean rank over the answers where the brand is named, ranks 1 to 10, with no penalty when the brand is absent, as today

criteria.text: Given natural competitive answers, When AI Choice is computed for a brand, Then it is (Chosen + Conditional) divided by the counted competitive answers, so the AI Choice of the brands of one question no longer adds up to 100%; for a competitor (Brand Rankings, matrices, Excel) the denominator stays all counted competitive answers of the scope, as today
criteria.given: natural competitive answers
criteria.when: AI Choice is computed for a brand
criteria.then: it is (Chosen + Conditional) divided by the counted competitive answers, so the AI Choice of the brands of one question no longer adds up to 100%; for a competitor (Brand Rankings, matrices, Excel) the denominator stays all counted competitive answers of the scope, as today

criteria.text: Given any view, export or AI summary that reads whether the brand won a competitive answer (question status, Excel favorability and row colour, competitive improvements, AI Citation Sources competitive losses, executive and perception summaries), When it reads a natural answer, Then Chosen and Conditional count as a win and Not chosen and Overlooked as a loss, as in AI Choice and Target Sources
criteria.given: any view, export or AI summary that reads whether the brand won a competitive answer (question status, Excel favorability and row colour, competitive improvements, AI Citation Sources competitive losses, executive and perception summaries)
criteria.then: Chosen and Conditional count as a win and Not chosen and Overlooked as a loss, as in AI Choice and Target Sources

criteria.text: Given AI Choice values, When the competitive improvements are detected, Then they use the same thresholds on AI Choice as today (an issue under 50%, Critical under 25%, Warning under 40%)
criteria.given: AI Choice values
criteria.then: they use the same thresholds on AI Choice as today (an issue under 50%, Critical under 25%, Warning under 40%)

criteria.text: Given AI Choice values, When the Brand and Category Prioritization matrices are drawn, Then their Y axis stays AI Choice, and the quadrant lines (Visibility 50, AI Choice 50, as since GEO-1524) and the AI Choice quality bands (Good above 50, Fair from 25) stay, reviewed on the first analysis runs with natural answers
criteria.given: AI Choice values
criteria.when: the Brand and Category Prioritization matrices are drawn
criteria.then: their Y axis stays AI Choice, and the quadrant lines (Visibility 50, AI Choice 50, as since GEO-1524) and the AI Choice quality bands (Good above 50, Fair from 25) stay, reviewed on the first analysis runs with natural answers

criteria.text: Given a competitive answer, When Target Sources selects gap answers, Then Not chosen and Overlooked answers are gap answers, and Conditional answers are not
criteria.given: a competitive answer
criteria.then: Not chosen and Overlooked answers are gap answers, and Conditional answers are not

criteria.text: Given natural visibility and competitive answers, When Share of Voice is computed, Then both count the same way: each brand family counts once per answer however many of its products are named, and the denominator is the number of brand families each answer names, not a fixed 10 per visibility answer (eg: Brooks, ASICS, HOKA, Saucony, New Balance in one answer gives Brooks 1 of 5; a competitive answer that names my brand and 2 others gives my brand 1 of 3, whatever its outcome), so the Share of Voice of all brands adds up to 100%, on every analysis date; the Share of Voice tooltip (today "Nike Air Max and Nike Pegasus ... that's 2 mentions", new text in GEO-1498 story 1.7) and the definition given to the AI summaries change to match, including the dates collected before this change
criteria.given: natural visibility and competitive answers
criteria.then: both count the same way: each brand family counts once per answer however many of its products are named, and the denominator is the number of brand families each answer names, not a fixed 10 per visibility answer (eg: Brooks, ASICS, HOKA, Saucony, New Balance in one answer gives Brooks 1 of 5; a competitive answer that names my brand and 2 others gives my brand 1 of 3, whatever its outcome), so the Share of Voice of all brands adds up to 100%, on every analysis date; the Share of Voice tooltip (today "Nike Air Max and Nike Pegasus ... that's 2 mentions", new text in GEO-1498 story 1.7) and the definition given to the AI summaries change to match, including the dates collected before this change

criteria.given: the new Share of Voice values
criteria.then: they stay Good above 25, Fair from 15 to 25 and Poor under 15, and they are reviewed on the first analysis runs with natural answers

criteria.text: Given a natural perception answer, When its themes are extracted, Then each theme gets a polarity (positive, mixed or negative) and an internal score that is never displayed, so the concept classification, the frequency and the category Sentiment tile work as today and the display follows Simplify Key Concepts (GEO-1068)
criteria.given: a natural perception answer
criteria.then: each theme gets a polarity (positive, mixed or negative) and an internal score that is never displayed, so the concept classification, the frequency and the category Sentiment tile work as today and the display follows Simplify Key Concepts (GEO-1068)

criteria.text: Given a perception answer that misreads the question or where the engine says it knows little about the brand, When it is parsed, Then it is parsed like any other answer, with no special behaviour
criteria.given: a perception answer that misreads the question or where the engine says it knows little about the brand
criteria.then: it is parsed like any other answer, with no special behaviour

userStory.want: the engines we already track collected as a real user sees them

stories.context:
✅ **Ready for dev** (2026-10-30) — wave 2. Build and staging captures with the Cloro dev key approved by the PM on 2026-10-30 (comment on this ticket); the switch to rendered capture in production still waits for the legal sign-off and the capture vendor contract.



**Acceptance Criteria**

- Given an already-tracked engine whose surface is public and no-login, When collection runs after the switch, Then its answer is obtained by rendered capture rather than an API call
- Given a captured answer, When it is stored, Then it is stored raw with its capture time and its locale, and can be read again later without capturing it again
- Given an answer, When it is recorded, Then the collection route actually used (rendered interface or API) and the vendor are stored with it; the route of each engine is set in production, and an answer collected through the API fallback (story 1.12) stores the API route
- Given a rendered answer, When it is stored for parsing, Then the widget text and markup the capture leaves in it are removed first (eg: "Let me narrow it down for you", "Go to product viewer dialog"), and parsing never relies on markdown created by a capture vendor
- Given a capture attempt that fails, When it ends, Then the failure is recorded, no partial answer is stored, and the answer is collected through the API fallback (story 1.12)

**Also delivered here (User Story 1.12 AC1):** Given an engine on rendered capture, When a surface is captured, Then it goes through one capture vendor, behind a layer that lets the vendor be changed later without changing how answers are stored or parsed

**Delivered elsewhere:** AC3 route and vendor columns → STORY-50.1 (GEO-1550); AC5 API fallback → STORY-50.12.

userStory.want: each country still captured in its own locale

stories.context:
✅ **Ready for dev** (2026-10-30) — wave 2. Build and staging captures with the Cloro dev key approved by the PM on 2026-10-30 (GEO-1558); the switch to rendered capture in production still waits for the legal sign-off and the capture vendor contract. Depends on STORY-50.9 (GEO-1558).



**Acceptance Criteria**

- Given a prompt configured for a country, When rendered capture runs, Then it returns the answer served in that country, as the API route did
- Given the same prompt across several countries, When it is captured, Then each country's answer is stored and attributed to its country
- Given an engine on its API route, natural or fallback, When the question is sent, Then the country goes through the engine's own country parameter where a staging check shows it reaches the engine, otherwise through the country hint "The user is located in {country}" as the only system instruction, never both, with no instruction on sources (today's "Prioritize {country}-language sources" goes), and the question is sent bare, with no "Market:", "Question:" or "Category:" line, as a real user would not type them _(updated by the PM on 2026-10-30; delivered by STORY-50.1, GEO-1550)_
- Given rendered capture, When a country is targeted, Then it uses the capture vendor's country setting and no instruction is added
- Given the capture vendor cannot target a country for an engine, When that engine is collected in that country, Then it uses the API fallback (story 1.12)


---

**Dev done (2026-11-05) — in review.** Branch `feature/GEO-1560-per-country-capture` → `feature/GEO-678-vague-2`.

**Functional ACs (Given / When / Then)**

**AC1 — Answer of the country**

- Given: a prompt configured for a country
- When: rendered capture runs
- Then: it returns the answer served in that country, as the API route did

**AC2 — One answer per country**

- Given: the same prompt across several countries
- When: it is captured
- Then: each country's answer is stored and attributed to its country

**AC3 — Country parameter, or the hint, on the API route** _(delivered by 50.1)_

- Given: an engine on its API route, natural or fallback
- When: the question is sent
- Then: the country goes through the engine's own country parameter where it reaches the engine, otherwise through the hint "The user is located in {country}", never both, and the question is sent bare

**AC4 — Vendor country setting, no instruction**

- Given: rendered capture
- When: a country is targeted
- Then: it uses the capture vendor's country setting and no instruction is added

**AC5 — Country the vendor cannot target**

- Given: the capture vendor cannot target a country for an engine
- When: that engine is collected in that country
- Then: it uses the API fallback (story 1.12) — this story ends the capture as `COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED` without calling the vendor; the API fallback itself ships with 50.12

**Rules for QA:** the same prompt in two countries gives two captured answers, each on its own country with its own locale; the text sent to the vendor is exactly the prompt text; a country outside the engine's coverage (`FLINK_CAPTURE_COUNTRIES_<PROVIDER>`, Cloro mode only — the mock supports every country) ends with reason `COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED`; a country the vendor reports serving wrongly ends as `COUNTRY_MISMATCH` (Cloro reports none).

stories.title: STORY-50.12: Fall back to the API when capture fails

userStory.want: every prompt to get an answer in each run
userStory.so: a capture problem never leaves a hole in my analysis.

stories.context:
🔍 **Code review** (2026-11-09) — dev finished on `feature/GEO-1561-api-fallback-on-capture-failure` (from `feature/GEO-678-vague-2`). Earlier: ✅ Ready for dev (2026-10-30) — wave 2. Build and staging captures with the Cloro dev key approved by the PM on 2026-10-30 (GEO-1558); the switch to rendered capture in production still waits for the legal sign-off and the capture vendor contract. Depends on STORY-50.9 (GEO-1558) and STORY-50.11 (GEO-1560).



**Acceptance Criteria**

- Given an engine on rendered capture, When a surface is captured, Then it goes through one capture vendor, behind a layer that lets the vendor be changed later without changing how answers are stored or parsed _(delivered by STORY-50.9, GEO-1558)_
- Given an engine on rendered capture, When the vendor returns no usable answer (vendor down or disallowed, engine not reachable, capture failed or cut), Then the answer is collected through the engine's official API with the bare question and the country sent as in story 1.11 (country parameter, or the country hint where the parameter does not reach the engine), the same request as the natural API route, so the prompt still gets an answer for that run _(updated by the PM on 2026-10-30)_
- Given an answer collected through the API fallback, When it is parsed and counted, Then it follows the same rules as any other answer and keeps the API route, so QA and support can see which answers came from the fallback
- Given the API fallback also fails, When the run ends, Then the answer is not counted (story 1.6)

**Rules (for QA)** — checkable on staging with the mock vendor set to fail

- An engine on rendered capture whose capture fails: the question still has that engine's answer for the run, with route API, vendor OpenRouter and the capture failure kind in the stored data.
- The fallback request holds the question alone and the country, through the engine's country parameter or the country hint, never both (same as an engine on its API route).
- The fallback answer appears in the metrics like any other answer.
- When both the capture and the API fail, that engine's answer for the question is not counted and the analysis completes (row FAILED, route API, capture failure kind kept, API error in the error message).
- Each question gets one answer per engine and run, never two (one captured and one fallback).

**Technical Acceptance Criteria** (dev context, ignored by QA)

- **TAC1 — Fallback on each kind:** Given the mock vendor throwing each `CaptureException.Kind` and a stubbed OpenRouter returning a natural body, When a `RENDERED` message is dispatched, Then one SUCCESS event with route `API`, vendor `OPENROUTER`, `captureFailure` = the kind, and the 50.1 natural request was sent.
- **TAC2 — Both fail:** Given the mock vendor failing and OpenRouter returning 500 on every attempt, When the message is dispatched, Then one FAILED event with `captureFailure` set, after the API retries; the counter advances.
- **TAC3 — One event:** Given a capture that fails then a fallback that succeeds, and the same message delivered twice, When both deliveries are processed, Then one event is emitted and one `llm_responses` row exists.
- **TAC4 — Same engine only:** Given a failed Gemini capture, When the fallback runs, Then the call goes to Gemini's OpenRouter model, never to another provider.
- **TAC5 — Counted like any answer:** Given a snapshot with captured, fallback and failed answers for the same engine, When enrichment and the KPIs run, Then captured and fallback answers are read and counted the same way; failed ones are not counted; the fallback rows show route `API` and a `capture_failure`.
- **TAC6 — Breaker open:** Given the capture breaker open, When messages arrive, Then no vendor call, each goes to the API at once.
- **TAC7 — Time budget:** Given a capture that takes its full timeout then a fallback that answers, When the message is dispatched with the configured timeouts, Then the fallback event is emitted before the async timeout fires.

**Implementation note (user decision 2026-11-09):** the capture runs in its own Flink operator since 50.9, so a failed capture's question is sent back to the same engine's API dispatcher (its own rate limiter, breaker, retries and 300 s async timeout) instead of an API call inside the capture call. No timeout value changes. A `[CAPTURE_FALLBACK]` log line per engine is written at report finalisation.

stories.title: STORY-50.13: Compare each engine before switching it to rendered capture

userStory.want: to see how an engine's results change between its API route and rendered capture
userStory.so: the switch of each engine is decided with the facts.

stories.context:
✅ **Ready for dev** (2026-10-30) — wave 2. Build and staging captures with the Cloro dev key approved by the PM on 2026-10-30 (GEO-1558), so the live comparison runs on staging; the switch to rendered capture in production still waits for the legal sign-off and the capture vendor contract. Depends on STORY-50.9 to 50.12 (GEO-1558 to GEO-1561); reuses the comparison endpoint of STORY-50.4 (GEO-1553).



**Acceptance Criteria**

- Given an engine planned for rendered capture, When the same prompts run through both routes, Then a comparison of the parsed results is produced (brands named and ranks, competitive outcomes, themes and tone, sources)
- Given the comparison, When the switch of that engine is decided, Then the decision is taken per engine from the comparison, with no pass or fail threshold
- Given an engine not yet switched, When collection runs, Then it stays on its API route

---

**Implemented — in review (2026-11-09)**, branch `feature/GEO-1562-route-comparison` → `feature/GEO-678-vague-2`.

**Functional ACs**

**AC1 — Comparison of the parsed results**

- Given: an engine planned for rendered capture
- When: the same prompts run through both routes
- Then: a comparison of the parsed results is produced (brands named and ranks, competitive outcomes, themes and tone, sources)

**AC2 — Decision per engine, no threshold**

- Given: the comparison
- When: the switch of that engine is decided
- Then: the decision is taken per engine from the comparison, with no pass or fail threshold

**AC3 — Not switched = API**

- Given: an engine not yet switched
- When: collection runs
- Then: it stays on its API route

**Rules (for QA)** — the comparison is a report for the PM, not a QA check. QA checks only:

- An engine that has not been switched answers through its API route in every analysis (stored route API, no capture).
- On staging, with the capture limited to the comparison organisation, the other organisations keep the API route for that engine.

**Technical ACs** (dev context, not read by QA)

**TAC1 — Answer-level comparison**

- Given: two reports of two organisations with 3 snapshots each, where one prompt's API answer names A, B, C and its captured answer names B, C, D (tracked brand B: rank 2 and rank 1), and a competitive answer Chosen on one side and Conditional on the other
- When: the endpoint is called by a SUPER_ADMIN
- Then: for that prompt and run, brands in both = B, C; only base = A; only compare = D; tracked rank 2 / 1; outcomes Chosen / Conditional; the response holds no pass or fail field.

**TAC2 — Themes and sources**

- Given: the same two reports, with themes per country × category and sources per answer
- When: the endpoint is called
- Then: each country × category lists both sides' labels with polarity and the labels in both; each answer lists both source counts and the domains in both.

**TAC3 — Not switched stays on API**

- Given: every provider at its default route and `GEO_CAPTURE_ORGANISATION_IDS` empty
- When: a report is processed
- Then: no message carries `RENDERED` (50.9 TAC10 kept green).

**TAC4 — Staging guard**

- Given: `gemini` set to `RENDERED` and `GEO_CAPTURE_ORGANISATION_IDS` = organisation B
- When: reports of organisations A and B are processed
- Then: B's Gemini messages carry `RENDERED`, A's carry `API`.

**TAC5 — Roles and tenancy**

- Given: the endpoint
- When: called by an ADMIN, or with a report id that does not exist
- Then: 403, then 404; each report is read with its own organisation id.

userStory.want: the Corporate Reputation cards of an engine that answers naturally to show the sources it used, and those sources to count in Cited sources
userStory.so: I see where each card comes from, as for engines that answer in the structured way.

stories.context: Follow-up of story 50.14b (GEO-1557, question Q2), asked by the PM on GEO-1557 (comment 871807, 2026-11-03): « Let's show the sources used please [...] These sources should also count in Cited sources. » Scope settled by the PM on this ticket (comment 872446, 2026-11-04): « let's make the brand images sources count in cited sources and target sources please. No reextract for history ».

acceptanceCriteria.title: Sources on the cards
acceptanceCriteria.text:
**AC1 — Sources on the cards**
- Given: a natural Brand Image answer that fills one or more Corporate Reputation cards (Brand Image, Employer Brand, ESG / Sustainability, Leadership)
- When: the user opens the drill-in of one of these cards
- Then: the card shows the sources the engine used for that answer, as for an engine that answers in the structured way

acceptanceCriteria.title: No source on an empty card
acceptanceCriteria.text:
**AC2 — No source on an empty card**
- Given: a natural Brand Image answer that does not fill a card
- When: the user opens that card
- Then: the answer adds no source to it ("No data available" shows no source, as today)
acceptanceCriteria.given: a natural Brand Image answer that does not fill a card
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answer adds no source to it ("No data available" shows no source, as today)

acceptanceCriteria.title: Brand Image sources count in Cited sources and Target Sources _(PM answer 2026-11-04, comment 872446)_
acceptanceCriteria.text:
**AC3 — Brand Image sources count in Cited sources and Target Sources** _(PM answer 2026-11-04, comment 872446)_
- Given: Brand Image answers with search sources, from any engine (natural or structured)
- When: the user reads Cited sources on the Overview and the Target Sources list
- Then: their sources count, as those of the Visibility, Competitive and Perception answers
acceptanceCriteria.given: Brand Image answers with search sources, from any engine (natural or structured)

acceptanceCriteria.title: Structured Brand Image answers read like natural ones
acceptanceCriteria.text:
**AC4 — Structured Brand Image answers read like natural ones**
- Given: an engine that answers in the structured way
- When: the cards, Cited sources and Target Sources are read
- Then: the cards are unchanged; its Brand Image sources now count in Cited sources and Target Sources too (AC3), including on its past snapshots (sources already stored)
